issues.rationale: Removed the unrequested immediate-versus-longer-term taxonomy and now accepts any evidence-supported recruiting and retention organization.
Allows separate items for distinct authorization and administrative work, removes the once-at-highest-tier conflict, and removes the hidden rescheduled-authorization timing rule.
Actual ICD-10 chapter naming is now optional; the rubric scores M00-M99 range classification and separate clinical narrative or laterality assessment.

issues.rationale: Pass rows may leave Issue_Type blank or use N/A, while discrepancy and unresolved-evidence rows remain limited to the instructed Issue_Type vocabulary.
Requires all vendor × CR-001 through CR-010 checks, explicitly distinguishes preferred CR-007, and limits automatic Critical severity to Mandatory = YES failures.
Added resolution_days for completed warranty dispositions and an explicit unresolved value for pending claims.
The pass-rate method must be disclosed, use only applicable requirement checks, and state the treatment of Verification Required; equivalent consistent methods remain acceptable.
PASS, FAIL, or PARTIAL is enforced only for applicable product assessments; N/A or a documented blank is accepted for non-applicable cells.
Applicable internal SKU and service rates are now mandatory when present; estimates are limited to missing items and require a documented basis and uncertainty.
Split the original three broad rows into six narrower rows with weights 10, 12, 8, 8, 8, and 10 while preserving the task total of 96.

The rubric correctly requires source-grounded engineering calculations. Supplying source extracts or deterministic controls to the judge is an evaluator-context change, not a rubric-content fix; no hidden quantities or prices were added.
Applicant and workforce source tables must be supplied to the evaluator rather than encoded as hidden outcomes in the rubric.
Normalized application, bulletin, correspondence, history, and public-lookup records belong in judge context or deterministic checks; the rubric retains supported DENY versus HOLD flexibility.
Rate, budget, payer, and peer extracts are evaluator inputs. Embedding top codes, peer values, or monthly conclusions would recreate hidden expected answers.
Referral rows and reference excerpts must be passed to the judge or checked deterministically; they were not encoded into rubric text.
Conditional-format rules and overlap behavior require workbook inspection or rendering. The visible-format requirement remains valid and was not replaced with hidden referral IDs.
Requisition, quote, compliance, history, and amendment extracts must be made available to the evaluator; vendor-specific answer keys were not added.
Replaced unverifiable template-provenance checks with observable bid-tabulation and scorecard structure, fields, calculations, and comparability requirements.
RFQ, catalog, site, pricing, quote, and external data-sheet excerpts must be supplied to the evaluator; no product certifications, prices, or conclusions were hard-coded.
DOCX page count requires pagination-aware rendering or metadata. The explicit 1–2 page task requirement remains, and no arbitrary word-count substitute was introduced.
